method: Direct visual inspection by root of actual front, right-side and rear neutral authoring images, after checking their manifest hashes.

findings.observation: The thin side jaw ends above a broad unattached-looking forward lamina. The separate strips and empty space interrupt the intended cheek opening and neck connection.
A wide straight horizontal band interrupts the flowing folded-wing plate courses; front view also exposes broad bare shoulder/mantle areas.

The back remains a broad simple panel field with large pointed inset shapes; the rear neck/skull has an exposed dark channel. Rear construction is a proposal and cannot be called resolved from front/three-quarter views.

sourceDiagnosis.attributionLimit: Current Python modules explain plausible construction causes but were not individually hashed in the render manifest. Exact module-to-render attribution is unproven.
sourceDiagnosis.breast: Body course z bounds overlap, but pointed tips/narrow angular keel and fragmented flank columns can leave gaps away from centerline. Extend local lower tip coverage while retaining course roots and silhouette; review collisions.
sourceDiagnosis.mantle: Blade width tapers after t=.62 to 6% at tip over a recessed shell. Delay taper/retain modest terminal width only after bilateral fold/guard/thrust clearance review; proximal and distal plates have separate owners.
sourceDiagnosis.neck: Upper throat lamina and cheek bands occupy adjacent heights with independent neck/head owners. A local central forward-contour trim needs jaw-open/head-pitch review to avoid a new exposed gap.

limits: Static qualitative review, not dimensional metrology.
No full collision, era eligibility, movement, performance or owner acceptance conclusion.
Rear anatomy is inferred where controlling references do not show it.
